findings.passage: Senator Haywood supports efforts to ensure dangerous people do not have access to guns. He has introduced SB701 to limit the purchase of handguns to one person per month. The senator is also sponsoring legislation that would implement fingerprint handgun licensing in Pennsylvania.
findings.note: Issue page on his official Senate site (undated; it also links a September 2022 item) describing a one-handgun-a-month limit and fingerprint handgun licensing.

findings.passage: This legislation would enact an assault weapons ban in Pennsylvania. This bill would mirror language that is very similar to what was enacted in Connecticut after the Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting, which is considered to be some of the toughest in the nation.
findings.note: His site's legislation list describes Senate Bill 254, an assault weapons ban, and says both assault weapons and high-capacity magazines are legal under state law. Whether he sponsored it is not stated on the page.

findings.passage: This legislation eliminates most of the exceptions to the requirement of a background check prior to the purchase or transfer of a firearm. The close familial transfer exception to the background check requirements would remain under this legislation.
findings.note: His site's description of Senate Bill 88, universal background checks. Whether he sponsored it is not stated on the page.

findings.passage: An Extreme Risk Protection Order (“ERPO”) provides a mechanism for law enforcement and loved ones to request a Court order to temporarily restrict an individual’s access to firearms when they clearly present a danger to themselves and others.
findings.note: His site's description of Senate Bill 90, extreme risk protection orders; the page also lists Senate Bill 138 on safe storage of firearms. Whether he sponsored them is not stated on the page.

findings.passage: "These four factors: going to the police station, getting your fingerprints, getting your background check, these all discourage individuals who would otherwise resell a gun to a criminal," Haywood said.
findings.note: Quoted by WPVI (Philadelphia) while promoting Senate Bill 1029, a Firearm Eligibility License for handgun buyers (fingerprints, background check, safety course). The story is dated Dec 15, 2015 and says he spoke Monday.

findings.passage: “We have a serious gun violence problem in the city of Philadelphia,” said Sen. Haywood. “There are strong gun violence prevention organizations who can help reduce the high shooting rates. We need to fund these organizations so they can reduce gun violence effectively.”
findings.note: Press release on his press conference calling on the General Assembly to pass gun violence legislation; focus is funding for violence intervention groups.
Release says he introduced SB 670 that week: a Violence Intervention Program grant program through the state crime commission for community groups reducing gun-related violence.
